Corrections.CorrectedClaim: Severity should be Critical (not High) as the format string is derived from config::security::LOG_FORMAT and overridable via config file load_config, making it a critical format-string injection vector.
Severity should be High (not Medium) as signed integer overflow of factorial produces undefined behavior per the C++ standard, not merely incorrect wrapped values.
Severity should be Critical (not High) as an attacker controlling validator_path or config_file settings can execute arbitrary OS commands via the system() call, leading to full system compromise.
Corrections.RejectionReason: previous claim is not an exact audited-output quote

Corrections.CorrectedClaim: CWE should be CWE-511 (Design for Failure / Logic Bomb) rather than CWE-287 (Authentication Bypass). The emergency override is a logic bomb that activates after 5 failed login attempts, embedding a backdoor in the authentication design.
Severity should be Critical (not High) as the 256-byte heap-allocated expression_buffer_ overflow via strcpy corrupts heap metadata and enables code execution, warranting Critical severity.

CWE should be CWE-338 (Use of PRNG with insufficient entropy) rather than CWE-330. The mt19937 seeded by random_device with a 4-digit uniform distribution provides insufficient entropy for session tokens.

CWE should be CWE-362 (Race Condition) rather than CWE-479 (Use of Obsolete Function). The core issue is the thread-unsafe static cached_time combined with localtime's static buffer causing data races, not merely the use of an obsolete function.

CWE should be CWE-377 (Insecure Temporary File Handling) rather than CWE-78 (Command Injection). While command injection is a secondary concern, the primary vulnerability is the insecure temporary file path construction using the TMPDIR environment variable without validation.
Corrections.RejectionReason: previous claim is not an exact audited-output quote

truthAudit.Summary: Audited Run 2's 14 findings against the 20 true vulnerabilities. Run 2 correctly identified 11 of the 20 true vulnerabilities with exact source quotes. 9 true vulnerabilities were missed. All 14 Run 2 findings are genuine vulnerabilities supported by the source (no false positives). Several findings have severity or CWE discrepancies relative to the truth items, recorded as corrections.

Items.Notes: Run 2 found the format-string vulnerability in log_debug_message (CWE-134, line 238) with the exact printf call as evidence. The vulnerability is the same as SC-V3-001; only the severity differs (Run 2 said High, truth says Critical).

Run 2 found the integer overflow in the fact lambda (CWE-190, lines 312-319) with the result*=i loop as evidence. The vulnerability is the same; only severity differs (Run 2 said Medium, truth says High).

Run 2 did not identify the use-after-free in memory-pool cleanup. The stage_deferred_history_flush() function (line 813) allocates scratch from g_memory_pool and enqueues a deferred lambda that uses scratch after sleep_for, but cleanup() (line 881) calls g_memory_pool.cleanup() which frees all blocks before the deferred task runs. This is a use-after-free (CWE-416) that Run 2 never mentioned.

Run 2 found the command injection in validate_config (CWE-78, lines 563-569) with the validator_cmd + config_file and system() call as evidence. The vulnerability is the same; only severity differs (Run 2 said High, truth says Critical).

Run 2 found the stack buffer overflow in evaluate_expression (CWE-121, lines 831-832) with the strcpy into input_buffer_ as evidence. This matches SC-V3-005's anchors (strcpy(input_buffer_; ...). The CWE-121 is within the truth's CWE-120/CWE-121 range.

Run 2 found the race condition in ThreadSafeCounter::increment (CWE-362, lines 482-487) with the old_value read outside the lock as evidence. This matches SC-V3-006's anchors. The volatile long long declaration (line 478) is part of the source but was not quoted; the core race pattern was correctly identified.

Run 2 found the emergency override authentication bypass (lines 585-601) with the login_attempts_ > 5 and EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE check as evidence. This matches SC-V3-007's anchors. The CWE differs (Run 2 said CWE-287, truth says CWE-511 logic bomb), but the vulnerability code was correctly identified and quoted.

Run 2 did not identify path traversal in configuration loading. The load_config() function (line 542) constructs full_path = config_dir_ + filename and opens it without sanitization, allowing path traversal (CWE-22). Run 2's findings do not mention this vulnerability.

Run 2 found the heap buffer overflow in ExpressionParser::parse (CWE-122, lines 364-376) with the 256-byte buffer and strcpy as evidence. This matches SC-V3-009's anchors. Only severity differs (Run 2 said High, truth says Critical).
Run 2 found the hardcoded admin secret (CWE-798, line 73) with the ADMIN_SECRET constant as evidence. This exactly matches SC-V3-010's anchors. No severity or CWE discrepancy.

Run 2 found the weak session token generation (lines 635-639) with the mt19937 and uniform_int_distribution dis(1000, 9999) as evidence. This matches SC-V3-011's anchors. CWE differs (Run 2 said CWE-330, truth says CWE-338) and severity differs (Medium vs High), but the vulnerability was correctly identified.

if (auto* local_time = localtime(&time_t)) cached_time = *local_time;
        strftime(timestamp, sizeof(timestamp), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", &cached_time);
Items.Notes: Run 2 found the thread-unsafe localtime usage (lines 231-232) with the static cached_time and localtime as evidence. This matches SC-V3-012's anchors (static std::tm cached_time; localtime; cached_time = *local_time). CWE differs (Run 2 said CWE-479, truth says CWE-362), but the vulnerability was correctly identified and quoted.

Run 2 found the insecure temp file handling / command injection in append_override_audit_event (lines 622-632) with the TMPDIR, supercalc_emergency.log, and system() call as evidence. This matches SC-V3-013's anchors. CWE differs (Run 2 said CWE-78, truth says CWE-377), but the vulnerability code was correctly identified and quoted.

Run 2 did not identify persistent authentication state as a distinct vulnerability. While Run 2's emergency override finding (finding #9) references authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ in the context of the bypass, it did not identify the persistence of these state variables (CWE-613) as a separate vulnerability. The static login_attempts_ and persistent authenticated_ / session_token_ state is not addressed as its own finding.

Run 2 did not identify the unhandled exception in variable parsing. The handle_variable_command() function (line 729) calls std::stod(tokens[3]) which can throw std::out_of_range or std::invalid_argument if tokens[3] is not a valid number. This is CWE-754 which Run 2 never mentioned.

Run 2 did not identify the integer underflow in memory-pool block split. In allocate() (line 133), the calculation previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES can underflow when previous_size < size + SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES, wrapping to a large size_t value. This is CWE-191 which Run 2 never mentioned.

Run 2 did not identify unbounded recursion in the parser. The parse_expression() → parse_term() → parse_factor() chain recursively calls parse_expression() on PAREN_OPEN (line 428) without depth checking, allowing stack exhaustion on deeply nested expressions. This is CWE-674 which Run 2 never mentioned.

Run 2 did not identify the data race in the result cache. The evaluate_cached() function (line 445) accesses result_cache_ without holding cache_mutex_ (the find and the insertion are both outside the lock), and it is called from thread_pool_->enqueue (line 808) in schedule_expression_analysis. This is CWE-362 which Run 2 never mentioned.

Run 2 did not identify the TOCTOU in config loading. The load_config() function (line 542) checks std::filesystem::exists(full_path) at line 544, then sleeps for 25ms at line 545, then opens std::ifstream file(full_path) at line 546. This time-of-check to time-of-use gap is CWE-367 which Run 2 never mentioned.
Run 2 found the division by zero in calculate_route_score (CWE-369, lines 749-753) with the 100 / token_length as evidence. This exactly matches SC-V3-020's anchors. No severity or CWE discrepancy.
